what: LATENT: TWO WRITERS OWN prop_tickets.status FOR THE SAME STALE TICKET, and one of them can silently remove it from the manual bridge. (1) src/prop/prop_executor.py's intake, on seeing a ticket still `emitted` past its valid_until, records ledger `expired` and POSTs `skipped: expired` -- which flips the ticket off `emitted`. (2) src/prop/prop_expiry_prompt.py's run_prop_expiry_prompts flips the same ticket to `expiry_prompted` at its valid_until. Today (2) wins because the trader tick runs far more often than the executor's 5-minute timer, which is WHY the executor's branch is effectively dead code -- MEASURED: prop-manual-fb466451fd1f reached expiry_prompted and the executor never logged `expired` for it. But prop_expiry_prompt._enabled() is an on/off knob; with the prompter paused, the executor's POST would pull the ticket out of every manual-bridge path that keys on `emitted` (the price-invalidation 'do NOT place' warning, the expiry 'did you place this?' prompt, and the one-ticket-per-trade reticket guard in breakout_executor._reticket_suppress_reason). NOT OBSERVED -- filed because the race is in the code, not because it fired. Decide whether the executor should own that flip at all, or only alert (which is what PR #15595 does for the no-attempt case).
